summary.text:
Let me design the FB.

State: qForward, qReverse (previous scan outputs). first flag.

Semantics: At scan, inputs sampled, read pre-state q[k] (previous outputs), execute transition, observe outputs.

Rules:
- If Stop OR (ForwardButton AND ReverseButton) => neutral.
- If neither button => neutral.
- fwdOnly: if qReverse then neutral else Forward = TRUE.
- revOnly: if qForward then neutral else Reverse = TRUE.

Note qReverse is previous scan Forward/Reverse output. Let's check test reverse:

Step0: F=true. pre q=(0,0). fwdOnly & !qReverse -> Forward=true. Output Forward=true. q becomes (T,F).
Step1: R=true. pre q=(T,F). revOnly & qForward -> neutral. Outputs FF. q becomes (F,F)? Previous direction now neutral since output was neutral. Step2: R=true. pre q=(F,F). revOnly & !qForward -> Reverse=true. Good.
Step3: F=true. pre q=(F,T). fwdOnly & qReverse -> neutral. Outputs F,F. q=(F,F).
Step4: F=true. pre q=(F,F). -> Forward=true. Good.
Step5: none -> neutral. Good.

Ambiguous test:
Step0: both -> neutral. q=(F,F).
Step1: F only, q=(F,F) -> Forward true. q=(T,F).
Step2: F=true, Stop=true -> neutral. q=(F,F).
Step3: R only, q=(F,F) -> Reverse true. Good.

So state variables simply track previous outputs: qForward, qReverse.

Implementation straightforward.

Declaration:
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Task
VAR_INPUT
 ForwardButton, ReverseButton, Stop: BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
 Forward, Reverse: BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
 qForward, qReverse: BOOL;
 first: BOOL := TRUE;
END_VAR

No supporting objects needed. "first" not really needed since q init false.

Body:
VAR
 fwdOnly, revOnly: BOOL;
END_VAR

Logic:
Forward := FALSE; Reverse := FALSE;
fwdOnly := ForwardButton AND NOT ReverseButton AND NOT Stop;
revOnly := ReverseButton AND NOT ForwardButton AND NOT Stop;

IF NOT Stop AND NOT (ForwardButton AND ReverseButton) THEN
  IF fwdOnly AND NOT qReverse THEN Forward := TRUE;
  ELSIF revOnly AND NOT qForward THEN Reverse := TRUE;
  END_IF;
END_IF;

qForward := Forward; qReverse := Reverse;

That satisfies. Let's compile.
